History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
48-year-old man with 3-day history of acute watery diarrhea (5–6 times/day) after brief vomiting, now afebrile but weak and dehydrated; assessment consistent with viral gastroenteritis.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Acute onset watery diarrhea.  
• Onset/duration: Began 3 days ago; vomiting occurred on day 1 (now resolved); diarrhea persists.  
• Frequency/character: Loose, watery stools 5–6×/day; no visible blood.  
• Associated symptoms: Initial vomiting (resolved); feels dehydrated and weak; poor appetite; felt mildly febrile on first day but afebrile now.  
• Pertinent negatives: No abdominal pain, no current fever, no headache, no myalgia, no recent ill contacts, no suspicious food intake recalled.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: None identified; limited oral intake due to nausea/dehydration.  
• Systems review: Denies respiratory, cardiovascular, genitourinary, or neurologic symptoms.

Past Medical History:
• Asthma – intermittent; uses blue inhaler as needed.  
  – Medication: Short-acting β-agonist inhaler, dose/route/frequency not documented.

Social History:
• Lives alone.  
• Occupation: Software engineer; off work past 3 days due to illness.  
• Tobacco: Never smoker.  
• Alcohol: Social drinker, infrequent.  
• Recreational drugs: Not mentioned.

Family History:
• Father: Hypertension; deceased (bowel cancer, age unspecified, ~10 years ago).  
• Mother: Type 2 diabetes.

Physical Examination:
(Not performed – telehealth consultation; no vitals provided.)

Investigations:
None ordered or performed during this consult.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Acute viral gastroenteritis  
  • Plan:  
    – Oral rehydration: Encourage liberal clear fluids; purchase OTC oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte).  
    – Medications: Paracetamol as needed for fever/constitutional symptoms (dose not specified).  
    – Diet: Light diet as tolerated; resume solids gradually.  
    – Activity/work: Remain off work until diarrhea-free for 24–48 hours.  
    – Warning signs: Seek care if bloody stools, persistent vomiting, inability to keep fluids down, worsening symptoms, or fever develop.  
    – Follow-up: Reassess next week if symptoms not improving.

General plan items: None additional.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing but expected elements: Vitals, physical examination findings beyond history, detailed asthma medication dosing, complete medication/allergy reconciliation other than inhaler and NKDA.  
• Internal conflicts: None noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; minor hesitations but clinical content understandable.
